description: Read-only architecture audit requested by user. Compare PR #843 with refactor/webbridge; map shared runtime, pairing, status and credential boundaries; identify concrete provider coupling and existing reusable contracts before implementation. Preserve working mix.lock. Action reuse: not applicable to this audit because no executable operations change; assess reuse candidates for any resulting refactor.

comments.text:
Read-only audit completed against PR #843 base refactor/webbridge (local ref 1ad46a514e23605e9d9737cc64378113bf19bb4b), branch HEAD bde56a04a. Installed jido_chat_whatsapp revision 81994494603ee768fb829e401df4242310da4d3a matches retained working mix.lock. No source edits or tests executed. Scope: shared bridge/runtime/pairing boundaries, not exhaustive branch correctness review.

A. Executive model: saved WhatsApp uses existing bridge state, adapter child specs, generic supervisor, ingress routing and outbound delivery. Drift is primarily provider-specific preparation, status and host-binding knowledge inside generic layers, not a separate saved runtime.
B. Responsibility map: Bridge resolves common contracts/config; JidoChatBridge orchestrates adapter ingress/egress; BridgeSupervisor owns child start/stop/tracking; State serializes Chat and caches ingress status; package ConnectionWorker owns transport/connection generations; package PairingSession owns provisional onboarding; Engine Connect owns encrypted credential documents; LinkedDeviceConfirmation owns atomic connector creation/idempotency. Pairing and SessionStorage are small host callback adapters, not independent runtime implementations.
C. Dependency map: Bridge -> JidoChatBridge.SessionStorage is new concrete-provider coupling (bridge.ex:371). SessionStorage -> WhatsApp Storage.Runtime/Split and confidential Engine credential_document; Pairing -> WhatsApp PairingSession/Split and Engine confirm_linked_device; JidoChatBridge -> adapter selected from provider config, State, shared supervisor, NodeRouter. Dependencies use mixed module constants/application config and per-connector options; no dependency-resolution changes recommended without further investigation.
D. Contracts: adapter.listener_child_specs(bridge_id, opts) returns {:ok, specs} or {:error, reason}; sink_mfa enters shared chat processing. Lifecycle sink sends profile/attempt/status/QR via confidential Channels event; State validates live source and generation. Package persist callback yields receipt/storage/runtime and start callback invokes existing CommunicationBridge.sync_config_runtime. Common Jido.Chat.Adapter has listener_child_specs but no common pairing/status callback. Current WhatsApp adapter accepts linked_device/amarula/manual, rejects websocket; atom renaming alone breaks startup.
E. State map: saved connector/config and encrypted credential records owned by Engine/DB; volatile protocol session/sender_key owned by package Mnesia scope; provisional state owned by package PairingSession; chat subscriptions/deduplication owned by per-bridge State; listener PIDs owned by shared supervisor registry; lifecycle source/attempt/profile/QR cache now also held by State. QR must not become durable credentials or chat events.
F. Flows: enable/start -> JidoChatBridge.build_runtime_specs -> prepare trusted storage/options -> adapter.listener_child_specs -> shared supervisor State/listener. Message -> sink -> State/Chat -> Engine routing -> shared adapter reply. Pair -> authorized Action -> package session -> Engine atomic save -> package volatile seeding -> existing runtime sync. Status -> shared API with mode-specific auth/config lookup -> either auth-status polling or cached lifecycle presentation. Retry -> mode-specific API -> existing bridge.sync_provider_runtime.
G. Invariants: exact connector/profile scope, no persisted override of trusted storage, enabled/current authorization checks, atomic/idempotent confirmation, stop preserves pairing, stale source cannot overwrite current status, lifecycle never reaches chat handlers, restart/stop targets current listener, retained credentials remain encrypted. Transport being WebSocket does not remove pairing/storage requirements or possible reauthentication after saved startup.
H. Drift candidates: (1) common Bridge directly imports WhatsApp-backed SessionStorage for outbound profile; (2) linked_device mode controls transport selection, provider infrastructure, storage prep, outbound requirements and BO authorization/status; (3) status split between auth_status polling and event cache with source monitoring; (4) Pairing hardcodes provider whatsapp and package types while Engine confirmation hardcodes whatsapp and phone identity. Names suggest greater genericity than implementation. Existing BridgeSupervisor and CommunicationBridge have no diff against base and should remain the runtime pillars. Shared ListenerStatus and State are existing modules, not new parallel runtime modules. Avoid merging cohesive host callbacks into an already large bridge merely to reduce module count.
I. Coverage map (inspected, not rerun): runtime_test proves isolated profiles, duplicate rejection, current PID after restart, startup cleanup and control/message separation; lifecycle_test covers stale source/attempt/profile and refresh; lifecycle_delivery_test covers readiness retries versus authorization; storage_test covers trusted child options, scope, revoked bindings, RAM/durable split and failure latching; onboarding_test covers confirmation, owner scope, expiry and partial save/start; pairing_api_test covers exact connector and current operator auth. These tests constrain a refactor but do not prove a second paired provider works through the same seam. Storage child-spec test currently asserts concrete package layout; preserve behavior while evaluating that coupling.
J. Unknowns: full upstream status/auth compatibility across other adapters; precise minimal callback extension and migration; BO consumer compatibility when transport/auth are separated; whether deleting host helper modules is beneficial after call-site tracing. No claim of runtime defects. Recommendation: first remove upward concrete-provider dependency from common Bridge using established bridge resolution/connection-option ownership, then assess common status and optional authentication capabilities without new provider runtime modules. Preserve pairing and storage host boundaries. No implementation plan approved or begun.
Action reuse: no executable changes in this audit. Candidate refactor should reuse existing listener_child_specs, CommunicationBridge.sync_config_runtime, bridge runtime sync, PairLinkedDevice/ConfirmLinkedDevice and Engine credential_document; generic runtime plumbing remains local-only, no new Action/tool exposure. Findings recorded here rather than a new repository plan document.
